coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, no runtime rebase

function.inferred_label: tagged (3-way) count with unsigned saturating subtraction, capped by a field upper bound

behavior.arguments: rdi = a struct pointer; the single result is returned in rax; all comparisons are unsigned
behavior.formula: count(rdi) = umin(base, [rdi+0x28]) where base = [rdi+0x18] when [rdi]==0 (full 64-bit), base = usub_sat([rdi+0x10], [rdi+0x18]) when (low32[rdi])==1, else base = 0
behavior.tag_zero_path: [rdi]==0 -> rax = [rdi+0x18] at 0x22c3f37, then capped by [rdi+0x28]; return umin([rdi+0x18], [rdi+0x28])
behavior.tag_one_path: low32([rdi])==1 -> rcx = [rdi+0x10] - [rdi+0x18]; cmovae keeps it only when [rdi+0x10] >= [rdi+0x18] (unsigned), else rax stays 0 (saturating); then capped by [rdi+0x28]
behavior.default_path: [rdi]!=0 and low32([rdi])!=1 -> rax = 0 at 0x22c3f47; the cap step (cmovb against [rdi+0x28]) can never lower 0, so the function returns 0
behavior.cap_mechanism: each path loads [rdi+0x28] into rcx, does cmp %rax,%rcx then cmovb %rcx,%rax, i.e. rax = umin(rax, [rdi+0x28])
behavior.saturating_subtraction: the tag-one arm uses sub + cmovae so an underflow ([rdi+0x10] < [rdi+0x18]) yields 0 rather than wrapping to a huge unsigned value
behavior.tag_compare_note: emptiness/zero uses the full 64-bit tag (test %rax,%rax); the ==1 discriminant compares only the low 32 bits (cmp $0x1,%eax). A tag whose low 32 bits are 1 but whose high bits are set still takes the tag-one arm; a tag whose low 32 bits are 0 but nonzero overall takes the default arm.
behavior.output_shape: single unsigned qword in rax whose contract past the cap is not claimed
